_comment: Railway's own managed Postgres, referenced through ${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}},
so the customer's database is backed up by Railway rather than by us.
Railway has no object storage product, so blobs go on the service volume,
which specs/backend/relay/server.md permits for a single-node install.
Railway terminates TLS on the generated domain, so WEALD_RELAY_TLS is off
and there is no port 80 to open on this path.
WEALD_RELAY_ACCESS_SET is enforce and is never weakened by a template.
There is no startCommand. Railway runs one through a shell, and the image
is distroless, which has no shell by construction. The Dockerfile's
ENTRYPOINT already starts the relay with no arguments, which is the whole
of what a start command would have said.
